question: Does moving the emotion notes after the history let llama.cpp reuse its cached prompt and cut time to first word, without bringing back the prompt-v1 problems?

layouts.current: [system + notes] [last 6 messages] [user] (reply.py as shipped, prompt v2)
layouts.notes_last_stepped: as notes_last, but the history window grows 6 -> 8 -> 10 messages and cuts back to 6, so the prefix is stable between cuts

how: patched in at run time from the scratchpad (layout_patch.py); repo files unchanged. Replay: the 9 live lines as one conversation + 4 angry flat lines, seeds 1-3, model alone on the GPU. Benchmark: scripts/benchmark_latency.py main() (158 MELD test turns) twice per layout and model, via a config copy; the second pass also records each turn's reply stage (time after the final tag), which separates the reply model from speech-to-text noise.
scoring: same rubric as reports/phase5_reply_model_3b.json; layouts shuffled per item, but blinding is weak: the two notes-last layouts often give identical replies (17 of 27 for the 3B), so the odd one out is usually 'current'. Third-person regex hits were all false positives ('they're' = doctor's visits).
